statement: In 42 of 43 analysed books at least one spread carries story information only in the picture; 5 are wordless or have a wordless reveal spread and in several more the turning point, a rescue plan or the real cause is carried by the pictures alone. The level-3 Kottavi Raja tells everything in its text.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends shows only in the picture that the new friend now sits alone; the wordless book counts trivially and should not be weighed as independent evidence of the technique.
2026-10-15: Holds across all three sources: African Storybook (Bohlale: the giraffe is drawn before the text needs it; Chicken and Millipede: the size gap carries the joke) and StoryWeaver (Monu: the monsters exist only in pictures). Method rule m005 still applies: today's product is text and audio, so this is evidence for the illustrated product and for what text must carry when pictures are absent. Re-read 2026-10-15 measured only_in_image at 58% on 12 pages (below the 20-page threshold, still measuring); judging it now as information a listener without pictures would lose. 2026-10-20: the blind re-read measured only_in_image at 54% agreement over 24 pages (unreliable), so this claim is capped at LOW until the field is judged more consistently.
2026-10-28: all 9 new works support. StoryWeaver: in Get Down, Rocky! two of three rescue ideas (box tower, ramp) are drawn, never told; in The Lost Ball each 'no' page shows a corner of the room tidied, which the text names only at the turn, and the ball shows at the box's edge before it is found. Book Dash: Who Ate My Hat and Clever Pig let the reader know before the hero (hat under the zebra's flowers; piglets hidden in the bushes). Today's blind re-read of Amo scored only_in_image at 67% (8/12); the field is still unreliable over 36 pages (58%), so the cap stays. m005: no proposal while stories are text-only. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-10-28 older-book observation, NOT counted (SOURCES.md keeps populations apart): Millions of Cats (Internet Archive, 1928, Gág, study_only) supports (hills drawn as textures of cats, the drunk pond, the end of the couple's loneliness only in the last picture).
2026-11-13: +10 support. Strongest: Going Places (the text never says the children are reading until p11), Alex's Super Medicine (each failure is one cry; the cause is only drawn), Banzi's Busy Bees (the real cause of the bees' return is shown, never said), Sweet Dreams (only the waking picture shows the rooftop and that the dream cat is his own). Re-read 2026-11-13 scored only_in_image 10/12 on Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.suggested: Hypothesis for illustrated stories: leave one fact per story to the picture; not applicable to text-only stories.
